title: Separable polynomials and squarefreeness over perfect fields
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $p\in K[X]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Call $p$ squarefree if $p\ne0$ and no square of a nonconstant polynomial divides $p$. If $p$ is separable [def-pc-separable-polynomial], then $p$ is squarefree. If moreover $K$ is perfect, meaning every algebraic extension of $K$ is separable, then $p$ is separable if and only if $p$ is squarefree. Constants and the zero polynomial are included.
